source.title: Topologically Densified Distributions
source.authors: Christoph Hofer; Florian Graf; M. Niethammer; Roland Kwitt

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different explicit regularizer and sub-batch construction affect held-out error after zero training error; it does not test the specific versions listed.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports test-error results for regularization methods and states that all approaches achieve zero training error. The lifetime plots and estimated mass results are related measurements, but do not measure the specific properties named in V7. Cited prior-work results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The theory assumes sufficient capacity to fit any training sample, drawing on Zhang et al., and the experiments evaluate representation regularizers. No result tests V1–V8. In particular, natural-label interpolation alone does not test V1; the batch comparison adjusts epochs to match update counts and changes batch composition, so it does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors prove a relative mass-concentration result under a connectivity condition and argue that it benefits generalization when reference sets have sufficient mass and their extensions remain inside the correct decision region. Their regularizer encourages this connectivity, produces the lowest mean test errors in the tested comparisons, and yields proxy evidence of mass concentration, stronger for CIFAR10-1k than CIFAR10-500.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a topological connectivity penalty to internal representations and constructs class-specific sub-batches; uses SGD with momentum. This differs from the memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, and example-removal methods in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test error varies by dataset and training-set size. The selected β also affects test error; the authors report that small validation sets track the test-error trend as β changes.

fits_no_version.finding: With zero training error, sub-batches plus topological regularization reduce mean test error from 7.1 to 5.6, 30.1 to 22.5, 39.4 to 36.5, and 29.5 to 28.5 percent across the four settings. Validation-selected beta also yields lower mean errors than Vanilla.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-wise topological regularization can improve held-out classification performance in small-sample image learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Sub-batch construction alone leaves mean MNIST error unchanged and lowers mean error on SVHN and both CIFAR10 settings; other representation regularizers have smaller or inconsistent improvements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The performance effects of batch composition and representation regularization depend on the dataset and regularizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 7 and 9 show representation connectivity transferring to test samples and stronger estimated mass concentration for CIFAR10 trained with 1,000 rather than 500 examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-wise representation connectivity can transfer to unseen data and accompany probability-mass concentration around training representations.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 108, 2020
record.problems: Experiments use small training sets and a single reported architecture per dataset. The authors state that mass estimates are relative to the reference set, and that the β-connectivity condition is encouraged as a regularizer rather than strictly enforced. Test-error table values are averaged over 10 cross-validation runs; hyper-parameter selection and validation procedures differ across rows.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 7–9 lifetime and estimated-mass results were not added as claim-version rows because they do not measure the properties specified by V1–V8.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and fixed-random-label experiments, random-label fitting measurement, or random-label held-out chance comparison.
No width sweep or comparison beyond the width required for interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; optimization uses momentum SGD.
No isolated batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets. Batch composition changes, and comparison-method epochs are adjusted to account for update counts.
No dropout ablation or dropout-rate sweep. Dropout is fixed within each architecture; its absence on MNIST is confounded with dataset and architecture.

No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, sharpness–generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Representation connectivity and mass concentration measure different properties.
No memorization-influence estimates or targeted example-removal experiment with random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: All 36 numerical values match Table 1. Their effect states cannot be interpreted as evidence for V1–V8, and the rows describe method evaluation rather than tests of those versions. Except for the validation-selected final method row, Table 1 reports minima selected using test error over hyperparameter grids. Figures 7–9 are already declared omitted and supply no missing test of a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy; the listed architectures and recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
